examples.name: Plain status row, no detail
examples.description: Omitting content renders a non-interactive row with no button and no popup.

examples.name: Click to reveal detail
examples.description: Providing content renders a real button; clicking toggles the popup below the row.
examples.jsx: <InlineMessage title="3 documents pending review" secondaryText="Last updated 2 hours ago" tone="warning" content="Review each document before the filing deadline on Friday." />

examples.name: Controlled, opened programmatically
examples.description: Reveal the detail automatically right after an action completes, via open/onOpenChange.
examples.jsx:
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<InlineMessage title="Saved" tone="success" open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} content="All changes saved." />

antiExamples.name: Hover-only reveal
antiExamples.jsx:
/* Don't build a hover-triggered version of this component */
<InlineMessage title="Hint" onMouseEnter={showDetail} />
antiExamples.reason: Popup's own guidance reserves hover-only reveals for Tooltip. Inline Message is click/keyboard-activated by design, so its detail stays reachable by touch and keyboard users too.

antiExamples.name: Wrapping trivial content in a popup
antiExamples.reason: Don't add an expand affordance nobody needs - omit content entirely for a message that has nothing more to say.
